units.text: The June 2022 HTTP standard classifies POST as an unsafe method, not safe. Multiple sources confirm safe methods are GET, HEAD, OPTIONS (and TRACE, QUERY in some listings), while POST is consistently listed under unsafe methods alongside PUT, DELETE.

judgement.reason: The passages consistently classify POST as unsafe and list safe methods including GET, HEAD, OPTIONS plus TRACE and QUERY, but none explicitly identifies the 'June 2022 HTTP standard' or dates the classification.

units.text: The assertion that POST counts as a safe method contradicts the cited HTTP standard definitions which explicitly exclude POST from safe methods.

judgement.reason: The passages explicitly list POST as a common unsafe method and state that POST, PUT, DELETE, CONNECT, and PATCH are not safe, so saying POST counts as safe contradicts them.

units.text: Official HTTP specifications and glossaries from June 2022 define safe methods as read-only operations; POST is classified as unsafe because it modifies server state through data submission.

judgement.reason: The passages define safe methods as read-only/no server-state change and list POST among unsafe methods, but they do not establish the June 2022 official specification context or state that POST is unsafe because it modifies state through data submission.
